quiz.question.text: In the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939), which side do you sympathize with more: the Republicans (Loyalists, Second Spanish Republic, International Brigades, etc.) or the Nationalists (Franco, Falangists, etc.)?
quiz.toll.communist.label: people killed worldwide by communist regimes
quiz.toll.communist.note: Scholars' estimates run from about 21 million to about 100 million, most of them the regimes' own citizens, many through executions, labour camps and famine. Sources: Benjamin Valentino, Final Solutions (2005); Stéphane Courtois and others, The Black Book of Communism (1997).
quiz.toll.fascist.label: people killed worldwide by fascist and Nazi regimes
quiz.toll.fascist.note: Including 6 million Jews in the Holocaust, during a world war that killed 70 to 85 million people. Source: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.

credits.lead: The posters and photos behind the question and the results come from Wikimedia Commons. Each one is in the public domain or shared under a Creative Commons licence. The copies on this site were made smaller, and the photos behind the results were turned grey. The emblems, the logo and the rest of the design were drawn for this site.

credits.image.rep-internacionales: Republican poster honouring the International Brigades, Spain, 1936 to 1938.
credits.image.rep-avant: Republican poster of a soldier, "Avant!" ("Forward!"), from the Catalan socialist party PSU and the UGT trade union, 1936 to 1938.
credits.image.rep-himno: Poster of the Spanish Republic's anthem, with the woman who stood for the Republic and its flag, 1931 to 1936.
credits.image.nat-barrer: Nationalist poster of a worker sweeping away the Republic's "enemies": communism, Freemasons, anarchists, regional separatism and politicians. 1930s.
credits.image.com-belomorkanal: Prisoners doing forced labour on the White Sea Canal, one of the first big Gulag building projects in the Soviet Union, 1932.
credits.image.com-perm36: The fence and guard tower at Perm-36, a Soviet labour camp for political prisoners that is now a museum, photographed in 2011.
credits.image.com-stalin-pipe: Soviet poster "Stalin's Pipe", with the "enemies" of the time drawn in the smoke, 1930.
credits.image.com-mao-poster: Cultural Revolution poster of Mao Zedong in front of red flags, China, 1960s.
credits.image.com-mao-tiananmen: The portrait of Mao Zedong on Beijing's Tiananmen Gate, photographed in 2014.
credits.image.fas-birkenau: The railway and gate at Auschwitz II-Birkenau, the Nazi death camp, photographed in 2007.
credits.image.fas-auschwitz-gate: The "Arbeit macht frei" ("work sets you free") gate at the Auschwitz I concentration camp, photographed in 2017.
credits.image.fas-nuremberg: The leaders of Nazi Germany on trial for war crimes at Nuremberg, Germany, 1945.
